question: A 12-year-old boy is brought in by his mother with a 2-day history of fever and generalized weakness. She says that her son was involved in a school fight with some other kids 4 days ago and sustained minor injuries to the face. He was otherwise well, until this morning, when he complained of pain in his right eye. Physical examination reveals periorbital erythema and edema of the right eye, along with ophthalmoplegia and proptosis. Which of the following findings will most likely be present in this patient on the affected side as a sequela of his current condition?

options.opa: Anesthesia along the CN V3 distribution
options.opb: Decreased vision with sparing of the optic disc
options.opd: Intact sympathetic innervation to the pupil, but not parasympathetic innervation

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Trauma to the face -> Orbital cellulitis -> Periorbital erythema and edema -> Ophthalmoplegia and proptosis -> Monocular diplopia -> 85% CHAIN: Trauma to the face -> Orbital cellulitis -> Ophthalmoplegia and proptosis -> Absent blink reflex -> 80% CHAIN: Trauma to the face -> Orbital cellulitis -> Ophthalmoplegia and proptosis -> Intact sympathetic innervation to the pupil, but not parasympathetic innervation -> 85%
analysis: The patient is presenting with signs and symptoms suggestive of orbital cellulitis, likely secondary to trauma from the school fight. The periorbital erythema, edema, ophthalmoplegia, and proptosis are indicative of an inflammatory process affecting the orbit. Given the involvement of the right eye and associated symptoms, the most likely finding on the affected side would be monocular diplopia.
